title: Effects of vagus stimulation by a slow deep breathing technique on the haemodynamics of intermediate coronary stenosis
summary:
In this study, the effect of a relaxation exercise in the form of a slow deep breathing technique (4711-method) on the autonomic nervous system will be examined. This breathing technique is intended to have a positive influence on haemodynamics, i.e. the blood flow in the coronary arteries. The aim of our study is to further investigate the underlying mechanisms of the positive effect of breathing exercises on coronary blood flow or heart function during cardiac catheterization in patients requiring pressure wire measurement. In addition the effects of resonance frequency breathing 
on heart rate variability will be assessed before, during, and after cardiac catheterization.

interventions.name:
Diagnostic test using invasive physiologic index (Resting full cycle) at rest with determination of the first and second measurement.

Performance of slow deep breathing 4711 and determination of the third RFR measurement. 

Performance of slow deep breathing 4711 and determination of the fourth

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Indication for cardiac catheterization with RFR-measurement
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnant and lactating women are not included in the study. Persons who are held in custody by court or governmental order will be excluded. Patients who are expected to have problems in conducting the study (dementia, alcohol/drug abuse, known autonomic polyneuropathy, persistent tachycardic atrial arrhythmias, ventricular extrasystole, other serious mental illness) will be excluded.
